beats: This pipe still has a hole. So why did the water stop?
The hole isn't plugged. Something is pressing on it harder than the water.
Inside, the water pushes outward, trying to lift the plastic away.
Glue? There's none. Is the plastic melted on? No, it peels right off.
Clue one: the ties. Pulled tight, a tie only pulls along its length.
But wrapped around a pipe, that pull bends inward, pressing from every side.
Clue two: the pipe is small. The tighter the curve, the harder it presses.
The same tie barely grips a tree, but crushes a thin pipe.
Clue three: the tie is thin, so the force lands on a narrow strip.
The answer: on this pipe, the ties squeeze six times harder than water pushes.
So the hole stays open, but the plastic stays pinned against it.
The water is still there. It just can't lift the lid.
Cogwise: how things work. Follow for the next one!
